newsitem.title: UK: UK years ahead of Europe in gas deregulation - Ofgas.
newsitem.headline: UK years ahead of Europe in gas deregulation - Ofgas.

text.p: Britain is at least five years ahead of the rest of Europe in liberalising the natural gas market and is pushing the continent to catch up, Clare Spottiswoode, director general of gas supply at regulator Ofgas said on Thursday.
"I would say we're at least five years ahead of Europe in introducing competition to commercial gas supply and even further ahead in introducing domestic supply," she said.

She added that Ofgas and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) were working hard to encourage other European Union members to liberalise their gas markets, but "it's proving a very tough task. There are plenty of nice words but when it comes to action it's a very different story."

She also told the official launch of the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE)'s new natural gas futures contract that the European Commission appeared to be stalling over plans to deregulate gas markets.
Ofgas is fully behind the new futures contract, Spottiswoode said, and she believes it is "a very important milestone in the development of the liberalised gas industry."
"We do believe it will bring big benefits to the whole gas community, not least price transparancy and confidentiality," she said.
Now that the futures market is fully functioning, Spottiswoode said Ofgas should withdraw from regulating it, and that finanical regulators should now take over.
